Most programming tutorials start by having you type something and promising it
will make sense later. That works for some people. For everyone else it
produces a year of copying code that runs without any idea why.

This series takes the other route. The first three lessons contain no Python at
all — they are about what a programming language *is*, what a computer is
physically doing when it runs one, and how to pick a language in the first
place. Once that is in place, the syntax stops being arbitrary and starts being
obvious.

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple" icon=false}
## You do not need to install anything

Every code cell in this series runs in your browser. Click **Run Code**, or put
your cursor inside a cell and press `Cmd`+`Enter` (macOS) or `Ctrl`+`Enter`
(Windows/Linux). Edit them, break them, run them again — nothing you do here
can hurt anything.
:::

## How to use this

Go in order if you are starting fresh. Skip to [Lesson 1](03-python-basics.qmd)
if you have written code before and just want Python.

Do not read it like a book. The cells are there because reading about a loop
teaches you very little and running one teaches you a lot. When a cell shows
you something, change a number in it and run it again to see what breaks. That
is the whole method.
